title: Proper integral exchange is invertible after residue reduction
statement: Use the coefficient construction [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients] and the same separated finite-type k-square and finite normed E/ℚ_ℓ hypotheses as in [lem-weil-pbc-integral-finite-exchange-comparison]. If f:X→Y is proper and the square is Cartesian, then for every bounded constructible integral complex M the derived reduction of its specified integral boundedConstructibleBaseChange component is invertible in the residue derived category.

source.place: Section 6.7, finite torsion proper base change, with Section 6.8 coefficient reduction

proof.text: Obtain the etale bounded-below complex L, functor F and arrow comparison from the finite exchange realization.

The residue ring is finite, so every element of ULift A has finite additive order. Apply Etale.isIso_baseChange_of_isProper_of_isAddTorsion_ring to the Cartesian square. This is the existing bounded-below torsion theorem, retaining the projective-line, prime and torsion assembly route of the blueprint unit.

A component of an invertible natural transformation is invertible, and every functor preserves isomorphisms. Transport that property from F applied to the etale component across the obtained Arrow isomorphism, using MorphismProperty.arrow_mk_iso_iff.

theorem integralExchange_reduction_isIso [IsProper f]
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (M : integralConstructible ℓ E X) :
    IsIso ((integralReduction ℓ E Y').map
      ((boundedConstructibleBaseChange (integralCoeff ℓ E) ℓ (sq.toCommSq.asOver (Spec (.of k)))).app M).hom)
